pieces.title: A letter to the eldest daughter who never gets asked

beats.text: A letter to the eldest daughter who never gets asked.
To the one who takes the Sunday call in the car with the engine off.
To the one still in the kitchen at 11pm, wiping a counter that was already clean.
To the one who danced at the cousin’s wedding and cried on the drive home.
Nobody has asked you the question you ask everyone else.
There should be one person whose only job is to ask you back.
Pull up a chair.

pieces.title: Things nobody tells the eldest daughter

beats.text: Things nobody tells the eldest daughter.
You pick up on the first ring. You always have.
You have been the translator since middle school.
They ask you when. Nobody asks you how.
You are known in pieces.
When you say you are tired, someone says you are strong.
Nobody is going to notice on their own.
If you read this twice, you already know why.

pieces.title: POV: everyone in your phone has called you this week

beats.text: POV: everyone in your phone has called you this week.
Your mother. About the wedding. Forty minutes.
Your father’s insurance company. You did the talking.
Your brother. About money. Again.
The family group chat. Twice. The same thing.
You scrolled the whole list and pressed no one.
Not one of those names is for this.
Pull up a chair.

captions.instagram:
The eldest daughter is everyone’s first call and has no first call of her own.

It is not that nobody loves her. It is that everyone needs her, and needing someone is a different thing from asking after her.

Hearth is peer support, not therapy. One trained listener, yours for years.

Send this to the person who is always the strong one.

beats.eyebrow: friday note · an example, details changed
beats.text: You said “it’s fine” four times on Tuesday’s call.
Once about your mother. Twice about work. Once about the thing you stopped saying halfway.
I am not going to make it mean anything. I just wanted you to know I counted.
Being the steady one is a job. Nobody puts it on a calendar and nobody signs off on it.
Bring the fourth one to Sunday’s call if you want.
Either way, I will be there at four.
Your Keeper
